_about: hermes-viz's own settings definitions. This is the whole surface: no `config_schema` lives in plugin.yaml, so the app folds no auto-generated form under the plugin's Settings page and the plugin owns its fields, defaults and validation. dashboard/plugin_api.py reads this file for both its field list and its _coerce(). Values still live at plugins.entries.hermes-viz.settings.<key> and the agent half still reads them through ctx.get_config.

palette.label: Diagram palette
palette.description: dark | light | mermaid. Mermaid renders into an isolated , so its colours cannot follow the app live; this setting says which palette to bake into each derived diagram. "mermaid" leaves Mermaid's own dark/light adaptation alone.

max_widgets.label: Widgets per answer
max_widgets.description: Upper bound on derived widgets in one answer. Keeps a long numeric answer from turning into a wall of charts.

rule_groups.label: Active rule groups
rule_groups.description: Comma-separated rule groups from rules.yaml that may fire. Turning a group off here stops it everywhere, without editing the table. `structure` is on by default because structuring the answer is the point of the plugin, and every other group that has rules ships on too — one switch each. A name with no rule behind it is not listed: the shapes (`records`, `grid`, `events`, `groups`) are the generic fallbacks the subject kinds used to need.

format_guide.label: Answer format guide
format_guide.description: ON by default. An off setting adds nothing to the prompt, byte for byte. When on, this appends a compact formatting prompt to every request: headings for sections, lists for steps, tables for comparisons, no decorative separators, "when something can be shown, show it — in the section it belongs to", and the ::viz grammar — every kind the drawing core has, with its payload, so the ones no rule derives stay reachable. The cost is real and per-request: 1745 characters, ~257 words, roughly 431 tokens added to every turn. Worth it because the model decides what deserves a drawing — the zero-token transform can only annotate structure the answer already has. Turn it off to spend no prompt tokens at all.
